subject: Make-good request: ACME POC extension + one-time credit — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Make-good request: ACME POC extension + one-time credit — exec approval needed

Team,

ACME Logistics hit a blocker in the integration window that materially reduced their evaluation velocity. They had planned a two-week spike test (to exercise routing + caching patterns) but one of their SRE hooks failed and they lost ~40% of the test runtime last week. They’re concerned the dataset we used for the PLG trial doesn’t reflect their production traffic and asked for a short make-good to keep momentum.

What I'm asking the Deal Desk/Leadership team for:
- One-time free credit: 1,000,000 tokens (to be consumed within the extended POC)
- POC extension: +30 days from today (so they can re-run the integration tests)
- Conditional conversion: ACME will commit to an initial Dedicated pilot if we provide the make-good and tests look positive (sales estimate: $480k ARR first 12 months).

Why this is strategic:
- ACME is a top-10 prospect in transportation vertical — strong reference value for logistics routing and returns optimization.
- Current PLG limits (free token cap + 14-day window) are what blocked them — not technical model quality.
- Close window: they’ll likely pause next week if we don’t show movement.

Attachments: ACME_POC_metrics.xlsx (perf/latency breakdown and the gap window). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4238.

Proposed guardrails if we approve:
- Credit expires 60 days from issuance.
- Token usage reporting turned on and shared weekly with our AM.
- No additional discounts beyond this credit; this is a one-time exception.

Markus — can Deal Desk provide standard wording and tracking for the credit? Laura / Rishi — would appreciate quick executive sign-off if we can. Sales asked I escalate now to avoid losing the window.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Make-good request: ACME POC extension + one-time credit — exec approval needed

Connor —

Thanks for the context and the metrics attachment. A few quick clarifying questions from Deal Desk before we loop execs: 
1) Has ACME already used any PLG credits against the current trial cap? If so, how much remains?
2) Are they asking for additional discounted list pricing, or strictly a term/credit extension?
3) Any legal/contract redlines expected (data residency, long-term support) — they’ve hinted at an on-prem pilot in Q2.

Operational notes: we can usually approve up to 250k tokens and a 14-day extension without exec sign-off. >250k tokens or >30 days needs leadership approval. If this is truly a make-good tied to a clear integration failure and high chance to convert, we can escalate.

I can draft a one-page MOU to warrant the one-time credit and the usage reporting. I’ll also add a requirement that conversion to Dedicated (pilot) is not guaranteed — we need a signed SOW.

Send the usage numbers and a capture of ACME's committed conversion language and I’ll prepare the Deal Desk package.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Deal Operations

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T12:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Make-good request: ACME POC extension + one-time credit — exec approval needed

Laura / Rishi — forwarding the short thread. Markus notes threshold policy below. Summary for execs:
- Ask: 1,000,000 one-time free tokens + 30-day extension.
- Rationale: integration outage removed sample traffic; ACME needs to re-run routing/caching tests.
- Commercial upside: estimated $480k ARR if we secure Dedicated pilot and conversion to paid in H1 next year.
- Risk: precedent setting on credit size; mitigated by one-time clause, explicit expiry, and mandatory reporting.

Alternative (if you prefer smaller ask): Approve 500k tokens + 30-day extension and require ACME to sign an Intent to Pilot (non-binding but indicates resource commitment).

We’re asking for a rapid decision — ACME leadership wants an answer prior to their vendor selection meeting on Dec 1.

Appended: ACME note (they’ve provided a short timeline) and the metrics file.

Connor

Connor / Rishi —

I approve a limited make-good on the following terms:
- One-time credit of 1,000,000 tokens (no further credits after this).
- POC extension: 30 days from issuance (issue date to be agreed with ACME).
- Conditions: weekly token usage reporting to Deal Desk; AM to verify tests are re-run and provide a short outcomes memo at the end of the extension.
- Commercial requirement: ACME agrees to enter a Pilot Intent document committing time/resources to the Dedicated pilot discussion within 30 days of completion. Not a revenue guarantee.

Please ensure Legal signs the short MOU language and Finance logs this as an exception for audit. Markus — please prepare the MOU and the tracking sheet; loop Legal and Finance. Connor — once MOU is ready, send to ACME with an explicit expiry date.

I want a note in the deal record describing why this exception was granted (integration failure, high conversion likelihood).

—Laura
